data.standardized_narrative: The gross claims development triangle indicates an overall strengthening of prior year reserves by $26.1 million, primarily driven by adverse development in the 2014 underwriting year, partially offset by releases from the 2011, 2012, and 2013 underwriting years. No specific causal factors for these prior year movements are explicitly detailed in the report.
raw_causal_phrases: The principal assumption underlying the liability estimates is that the future claims development will follow a similar pattern to past claims development experience.
This includes assumptions in respect of paid and incurred claims, claim handling costs and claim inflation factors for each underwriting year.

Additional qualitative judgements are used to assess the extent to which past trends may not apply in the future, for example: once-off occurrence; changes in market factors such as public attitude to claiming; economic conditions; as well as internal factors such as portfolio mix, delays in settlement, policy conditions, and claims handling procedures.
Judgement is further used to assess the extent to which external factors such as judicial decisions and government legislation affect the estimates.

Unforeseen changes may affect the suitability of that data and would be expected to have an impact on the accuracy of the results and increased uncertainty in the projections. Such issues would include unexpected claims inflation, shocks to the global economy, changes in legislation and the emergence of new types of claim.
data.data_quality_notes: The prior year development amount was calculated from the gross claims development triangle as no explicit prior year movement note was available. There is a discrepancy in the direction of total prior year development between the gross and net claims development triangles (gross shows strengthening, net shows release).
